study.title: Neuroinflammation-informed neuroimaging-transcriptomic signatures explaining acupuncture's therapeutic effects in chronic insomnia
study.randomization: yes, randomly assigned to either an acupuncture group or a waitlist group
study.blinding: not explicitly described; no sham arm included; participants in waitlist group received no treatment
study.population: Patients with chronic insomnia disorder (CID) enrolled in outpatient clinics of the Affiliated Hospital of CDUTCM and Chengdu Second People's Hospital from April 2022 to November 2022
study.inclusion_criteria: right-handed individuals of any gender, aged between 18 and 60 years; scored >7 on the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI); experienced insomnia symptoms (including difficulty falling asleep, maintaining sleep, or early awakening) at least three times per week for more than three months; had not taken any hypnotic drugs or other psychiatric medications within two weeks prior to enrollment; diagnosis based on ICSD-3
study.exclusion_criteria: history of consciousness disorders; other sleep disorders such as sleep apnea syndrome, sleep-related movement disorder, central disorders of hypersomnolence, and circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders; severe cardiac, hepatic, renal, cerebral, or hematopoietic system diseases; history of mental disorders including depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety, schizophrenia, or personality changes; pregnancy or lactation or those intending to become pregnant within the next three months; history of alcohol, drug, or caffeine dependence; contraindications for magnetic resonance imaging, such as the implantation of electronic devices or metallic objects

arms.dropouts: 1 patient excluded due to scheduling conflicts
3 patients excluded due to scheduling conflicts

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: bilateral stimulation for all except GV20 and Sishencong
interventions.laterality_exact: bilateral for Anmian, HT7, PC6, SP6; midline/single for GV20 and Sishencong
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.30 mm in diameter, 25 mm and 40 mm in length
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; 'Deqi' sensation (characterized by sensations of pain, heaviness, numbness, swelling, or radiation) was induced through needle manipulation techniques
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: two trained, licensed acupuncturists with over three years of clinical experience

sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: pain, heaviness, numbness, swelling, or radiation
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: The 'Deqi' sensation, a clinical marker of effective acupuncture characterized by sensations of pain, heaviness, numbness, swelling, or radiation, was induced through needle manipulation techniques such as lifting, thrusting, twirling, and rotating.
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi is described as intended/induced, but no quantitative sensory scores are reported

extraction_notes.note: Detailed neuroimaging results for all significant regions are reported in Table S2 (supplement), which was not provided with the PDF. Only the brain regions explicitly named in the main text could be extracted for the GBC contrast tables. Full coordinate or t-value data for all 83 regions are unavailable without the supplement.

No MNI coordinates are reported in the main text for any of the GBC results. Results are provided at the level of DK atlas region labels only. Coordinate-based neuroimaging synthesis will not be possible without supplementary tables.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success/allocation guessing were not assessed or reported. The authors chose a waitlist rather than sham control specifically to avoid sham placebo effects, and acknowledge this limits disentangling specific needling from contextual effects.
No adverse events section is present in the paper. The paper does not state whether adverse events occurred or were monitored.
Deqi and sensory responses were not quantitatively assessed or reported. The paper only states that Deqi was induced, with narrative description of intended sensations.
Peripheral cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, CRP) were collected only in the acupuncture arm, not in the waitlist arm, preventing between-group cytokine comparisons.

IL-1β baseline values for acupuncture group are reported as 20.1 (1.6) in Table 1, which is identical to the IL-6 baseline value. This may reflect a typo or OCR error in the table; both IL-6 and IL-1β baselines are listed as 20.1 (1.6).

The paper states GBC changes for the waitlist group included increases in 'right cingulate isthmus, right parahippocampal gyrus, and left paracentral cortex,' but notes these are at p < 0.05 uncorrected and refer readers to Table S2. The text also mentions 'Fig. 3d.' No additional specific regions were mentioned for the waitlist group in the main text.

The paper reports that the transcriptomic-imaging association analysis was limited to the left hemisphere (34 cortical + 7 subcortical = 41 regions) due to limited right hemisphere AHBA donor data. However, the GBC change t-value maps used in PLS-R are described as 'an average over the two brain hemispheres' in Figure 4 legend. This may create a spatial mismatch; details are in Supplementary materials not provided.

The paper describes that GBC was calculated using only positive correlations (Fisher's Z-transformed; mean of all positive values; negative correlations excluded). This is an important methodological note affecting interpretation of GBC values.

Cell-type enrichment results (astrocyte enrichment pFDR < 0.05; inhibitory neuron enrichment pFDR < 0.05) and GO enrichment terms are referenced to Table S3 and Table S4 in supplementary materials, which were not provided. Only the main narrative and Fig. 4d/4e results could be used for extraction.

The paper references gene TNAK with Z = −3.75 ranking 12,478/12,506 as a representative negatively-weighted gene in PLS1, but full gene lists and Z-scores for all 12,506 genes are in supplementary materials not provided.

The acupuncture treatment sessions were conducted over four weeks (20 sessions, once daily). It is unclear whether the post-treatment fMRI scan was conducted immediately after the final session or after a washout period. The paper states scans were conducted at 0 and 4 weeks.

The paper states a 20% dropout rate was anticipated in sample size calculation (target 24 per group), and final analyzed n = 23 acupuncture and 21 waitlist (total 44), consistent with reported exclusions. The paper also states 'No participant was excluded due to head movements during the fMRI scan.'
